questions.q: Which report-formula function plays the role of T-SQL's CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE?
questions.explain: IF(test, if_true, if_false) is the everyday conditional, and nesting IFs gives multiple tiers.

questions.q: Which tab of the formula editor is the best place to confirm a function's exact name and arguments?
questions.explain: The Functions tab lists the functions available for the formula type in your org's release, grouped by category.

questions.q: What do you get when you subtract one date field from another in a formula?
options: An error, subtraction is not allowed on dates
questions.explain: Date subtraction returns days, which is how ages and cycle times are calculated, for example CLOSE_DATE - CREATED_DATE.

questions.q: Which function is most similar to LAG() in SQL for comparing a group to the previous one?
questions.explain: PREVGROUPVAL returns the previous group's value at a grouping level, enabling change-from-prior-period calculations.

questions.q: Why are PARENTGROUPVAL and PREVGROUPVAL not useful in a row-level formula?
options: Row-level formulas cannot use functions at all
They only work on text fields
They are restricted to system administrators
They depend on the report's grouping structure, which row-level formulas do not have
questions.explain: These functions read values across grouping levels, so they belong in summary formulas on grouped reports.
